# Forensic Dossier — PharmaMar (PHM.MC)
*Sector: Healthcare · Signal type: deep_value · Single transcript available: FY2025 results call, 2026-02-27*

> **Evidence-base caveat (stated up front, not hedged):** The screener supplied **one** earnings transcript (FY2025 full-year call, 2026-02-27), not the up-to-8-quarter series this protocol assumes. A true *trajectory* of tone and credibility across quarters therefore cannot be reconstructed from the transcript alone. Where the protocol asks for evolution-over-time, I reconstruct it from the **5-year financial trajectory** the screener does provide (2021→2025 revenue / NI / EPS) and treat the single call as the current narrative snapshot tested against that trajectory. Every quarter-specific tonal claim below is anchored to the one dated call; every multi-year claim is anchored to the financials. I do not fabricate quotes from quarters I was not given.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The financials tell a violent boom-bust-reboot story that the single transcript catches at the top of the reboot. PharmaMar is a Spanish marine-derived oncology house whose entire equity story rides on **lurbinectedin (Zepzelca)** in small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), licensed out to **Jazz Pharmaceuticals (US)** and **Merck (Japan)**, plus legacy trabectedin (Yondelis).

The five-year trajectory shows the narrative arc better than any single call:
- **2021:** rev €230M, NI €93M, EPS €5.13 — a COVID-era peak (the company also sold an antiviral, Aplidin/plitidepsin, narrative).
- **2022–2023 collapse:** rev €196M→€158M, NI €49M→**€1M**, EPS €2.73→**€0.06**. The story nearly went to zero on the P&L — a genuine near-death earnings trough in 2023.
- **2024 stabilization:** rev €175M, NI €26M, EPS €1.49.
- **2025 reboot:** rev €221M (+26.6%), NI €75M (+187%), EPS €4.36 (+192.6%), EBITDA "roughly 5x versus '24."

So the FY2025 call is management narrating the *exit from a trough*, not steady-state compounding. The core story as told on 2026-02-27 has a clear spine: **(1)** the October 2025 US FDA approval of Zepzelca as **first-line (1L) maintenance** in SCLC (in combination with atezolizumab, via partner Jazz) is the franchise-transforming event; **(2)** the **EMA opinion for European 1L maintenance is "expected likely in the first quarter"** with possible EU marketing in H2-2026; **(3)** the **LAGOON** Phase III (2L SCLC) reads out top-line **H2-2026**; **(4)** earlier-stage shots — **SaLuDo** (sarcoma, results H1-2027), **PM54** and **PM534** (Phase I) — provide optionality.

Growth drivers *introduced*: 1L maintenance label expansion (the number-of-cycles argument — "about double from 4 to 8") and the atezolizumab-duopoly share argument ("Coke and Pepsi... interchangeable duopoly"). Growth drivers *quietly under pressure*: **US Zepzelca royalties actually fell 12% in 2025** — management attributes 7.5pts to EUR/USD and the rest to "a new competitor into the market." That is the single most important tension buried in an otherwise triumphant call: the franchise's existing royalty stream went *backwards* in the very year management is calling transformative, and the bull case requires the new 1L label to more than reverse that.

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim (2026-02-27) | Hard number | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Revenues grew 27% year-on-year" | Screener rev +26.6% YoY (€175M→€221M) | **Corroborated.** Matches almost exactly. |
| "net income up 187% year-on-year" | NI €26M→€75M = **+188%**; EPS +192.6% | **Corroborated.** Real, not adjusted-only. |
| "EBITDA... roughly 5x versus '24" | Not independently in the block, but NI +188% and net margin 33.9% are consistent with a large EBITDA step | **Plausible / consistent.** Margin expansion is real (net 33.9%, gross 94.5%). |
| "operating cash flow amounting to €53M"; "cash and financial investment of €168M" | TTM FCF €58M; net debt **−€120M to −€166M (net cash)**; Altman-Z 9.9; Piotroski 8/9 | **Corroborated and then some.** Fortress balance sheet. ROE 23.4%, ROIC 12.1%. |
| Zepzelca 1L is a "meaningful catalyst," sales "improved starting this year" | Consensus **fwd EPS growth +147.7%**; fwd revenue tailwind implied | **Forward-dependent — not yet in trailing numbers.** The market already embeds a near-tripling of forward EPS; the catalyst is *priced as success*, not as an open question. |
| Implicit: franchise momentum is up and to the right | **US royalties −12% in 2025**; 3-yr revenue CAGR only **+4.1%**; 5-yr EPS CAGR **−4.0%** | **Diverges.** The triumphant tone masks a flat-to-declining multi-year through-line. 2025 is a recovery to *below* the 2021 peak (EPS €4.36 vs €5.13), not a new high. |
| "first priority is investment in R&D"; €34M buybacks + dividend "decide on a yearly basis" | Net cash funds it; FCF margin 19.8% | **Corroborated.** Capital allocation is conservative and self-funded — a genuine deep-value support. |

**Where the story is richer than the numbers justify:** the *framing* of 2025 as a clean inflection. On a 3-year view revenue compounds at only +4.1% and EPS at **−4.0%**; the company is *recovering* a prior peak, not breaking out. The −12% US royalty decline is real evidence that the existing Zepzelca stream is contested by a new competitor — yet the call spends far more oxygen on the *new* label than on defending the *existing* one.

**Where the story is poorer than the numbers justify (i.e., management undersells):** the **balance sheet**. €168M cash / net-cash, self-funding a multi-Phase-III pipeline "without any pressure" (María Luisa's exact framing) is a materially better risk profile than a typical clinical-stage oncology name, and management states it almost in passing. For a deep-value lens, the solvency (Altman-Z 9.9, Piotroski 8/9) is the most underweighted positive in the transcript.

---

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Single-call rating: Confident–Promotional (snapshot, not a trajectory).** With only the 2026-02-27 call, I cannot rate rising vs. falling across quarters; I rate the *posture* of the one call and cross-check it against the multi-year financial direction.

- Opening tone is unambiguously **offensive/growth**: "a very strong year," "clear progress, both strategically and financially," "transformative year for the company." 
- Specificity is **high on dated milestones**: EMA opinion "likely in the first quarter," EU marketing "in the second half of this year," LAGOON top-line "in the second half of this year," SaLuDo enrollment "ahead of the schedule," PM54 data at "ESMO Congress in Madrid in October." Management is *willing to put dates on catalysts* — a confidence tell.
- But specificity **collapses to defensiveness on the hard commercial question.** When asked the single most important number — how Q4 1L US sales ("90 million sales in the U.S.") compared to internal expectations — the answer is a flat deflection: *"We're not going to tell you what our projections are and Jazz doesn't give you what their projections are... not much that I can help you with."* That is the offensive-to-defensive pivot, inside one call: bullish on the *narrative*, opaque on the *scoreboard*.

Net: the through-line direction of the business over five years is **down-then-recovering** (EPS €5.13→€0.06→€4.36); the tone of the call is pitched as if it were **steadily up**. The gap between the two is the central credibility question.

---

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Reliability: Medium.** Two cross-checks:

1. **Beat rate.** The financials show **beat 5/7 quarters (71%)**. That is a respectable, above-coin-flip delivery record and supports treating dated milestone guidance as more likely than not. It does **not** support treating it as bankable — ~29% of recent quarters missed.
2. **The structural credibility problem is that PharmaMar does not control its own scoreboard.** The economically decisive variable — US Zepzelca sell-through — sits with **Jazz**, and management repeatedly hides behind that: *"that's not something that we make public,"* and on Japan, *"this is the Merck task... It's not PharmaMar decision."* So even a perfect beat history on PharmaMar's own lines (royalties, raw-material sales, licensing) cannot validate the part of the thesis that matters most. **Guidance on the catalyst is therefore inherently un-auditable in real time.**

No evidence of deliberate sandbagging; if anything the FY2025 framing leans the other way (promotional). The honest read: **dated regulatory/trial milestones are credibly scheduled (Medium-High), but the commercial ramp that those milestones are supposed to unlock is opaque by design (Low auditability).**

---

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Even within one call, the pressure points are sharp and recurring:

- **"How is the 1L launch actually tracking?"** (Joseph Hedden, Rx Securities, on the $90M US number). **Deflected outright.** Management hid behind Jazz's non-disclosure and "inventory levels... not something we make public." This is the question that, if it later disappoints, becomes the bad-news vector.

- **Capital allocation discipline** (buybacks vs. M&A/in-licensing). Answered candidly ("we could do both"), R&D stated as first priority — analysts are watching whether the net-cash pile gets spent on a dilutive diversification deal.

The thread connecting these: **the most valuable information is structurally outside management's mouth** (Jazz's sell-through, Jazz's patent litigation, Merck's Japan timing). That is the defining analyst frustration with this name.

---

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 **US Zepzelca royalties −12% in 2025** — the existing core franchise revenue went backwards in the "transformative" year, with a named new competitor in the market. The bull case must out-run an already-eroding base.
